title: “Lord, let me never grow numb to mercy, nor casual with holiness. Teach me to live changed by what I have been spared.”
paragraphs: “Lord, let me never grow numb to mercy, nor casual with holiness. Teach me to live changed by what I have been spared.”
When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment.
Hidden within the ark, I do not speak. I do not act. I only see.

The storm roars with a force beyond human strength. The waters rise. The world I knew is being undone. From this place of shelter, my heart trembles—not with superiority, but with grief, awe, and the unbearable weight of holiness.
I am safe, yet shaken. Protected, yet undone.
What does it mean to stand within mercy while the world outside is lost—and how does that shape the way I live now?
